Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1c and 1d) demonstrate severe cystic and varicose bronchiectasis with a diffuse distribution that is most prominent in the lower lobes, which is the classic radiological pattern associated with primary ciliary dyskinesia. Upper lobe predominance is typically seen in cystic fibrosis, whereas PCD characteristically affects the middle and lower lobes.
